commit 0bfdb9c18b392eadb4260049548bec6a05e34095
Author:     Yukihiro "Matz" Matsumoto <matz@ruby.or.jp>
AuthorDate: Mon Jun 22 21:33:18 2026 +0900
Commit:     Yukihiro "Matz" Matsumoto <matz@ruby.or.jp>
CommitDate: Mon Jun 22 21:33:18 2026 +0900

    vm.c: prevent use-after-free when GC runs during a stack realloc

    Growing the callinfo stack (cipush) or the VM value stack
    (stack_extend_alloc) calls mrb_realloc, which can run an incremental GC step
    after it has freed the old buffer but before c->cibase/c->ci (or c->stbase)
    are reassigned. The GC then marks the freed stack through the stale pointers,
    a use-after-free reachable from mrb_load_string on ordinary source
    (ASan-confirmed in #6906). Disable GC across each realloc so no step observes
    the half-updated context.

    Co-authored-by: Claude <noreply@anthropic.com>

heap-use-after-free in `mark_context_stack` (`gc.c:659`) - callinfo stack realloc during incremental GC
### Summary

A `cipush` callinfo-stack reallocation that happens **during** an incremental-GC step leaves `mark_context_stack` reading a freed context stack - a heap-use-after-free. Reachable from plain Ruby source via `mrb_load_string`; ASAN-confirmed on current `master`.

### Version

```
master @ 7f035bb60 (2026-06-22)   # also confirmed at 01e1e2ba3
```
ASAN build (`-fsanitize=address`).

### Build configuration (to reproduce with ASAN)

`build_config/asan.rb`:

```ruby
MRuby::Build.new do |conf|
  conf.toolchain :clang
  conf.gembox 'default'
  conf.cc.flags      << %w(-fsanitize=address -g -O1 -fno-omit-frame-pointer)
  conf.cxx.flags     << %w(-fsanitize=address -g -O1) if conf.respond_to?(:cxx)
  conf.linker.flags  << %w(-fsanitize=address)
end
```

```sh
git clone https://github.com/mruby/mruby && cd mruby
git submodule update --init --recursive          # pulls Prism (mrbgems/mruby-compiler/lib/prism)
# carry ASAN in CC *and* LD so host tools (mrbc/presym) also link the ASAN runtime:
CC="clang -fsanitize=address -g -O1 -fno-omit-frame-pointer" \
CXX="clang++ -fsanitize=address -g -O1" \
LD="clang -fsanitize=address" \
  rake MRUBY_CONFIG=$PWD/build_config/asan.rb
ASAN_OPTIONS=detect_leaks=0 ./build/host/bin/mruby t.rb
```

### Reproducer

```ruby
(6..10).to_a.index{GC.malloc_threshold=4
def a =[]!=a
u=a}
```

```sh
$ ./bin/mruby t.rb
```

(The low `GC.malloc_threshold` forces frequent incremental GC so the race window is hit deterministically; the block body grows the callinfo stack via the nested call/`def`.)

### ASAN report

```
==ERROR: AddressSanitizer: heap-use-after-free ...
READ of size 8 at 0x51b000000668 thread T0
    #0 mark_context_stack   src/gc.c:659:17
    #1 mark_context         src/gc.c:688:3
    #2 root_scan_phase      src/gc.c:1095:3
    #3 incremental_gc       src/gc.c:1302:5
    #4 incremental_gc_step  src/gc.c:1346:15
    #5 mrb_incremental_gc   src/gc.c:1394:5
    #6 mrb_realloc_simple   src/gc.c:234:7      <-- realloc triggers the GC step
    #7 mrb_realloc          src/gc.c:246:8
    #8 cipush               src/vm.c:386:32     <-- ... while growing the callinfo stack
    #9 mrb_vm_exec          src/vm.c:2804:12
   #10 mrb_yield            src/vm.c:1353:10
   #11 mrb_ary_index_m      src/array.c:1601:22
```
comments https://api.github.com/repos/mruby/mruby/issues/6906/comments

COMMENT matz
Thanks again for another precise ASan report. There were actually two instances of the same bug: `cipush` (growing the callinfo stack) and `stack_extend_alloc` (growing the VM value stack) both call `mrb_realloc`, which can run an incremental GC step after freeing the old buffer but before the context pointers are reassigned, so the collector marked the freed stack. Fixed on master (0bfdb9c18) by disabling GC across each realloc. Your reproducer now raises a clean `SystemStackError` instead of corrupting memory. Thanks!

7023 vm.c: refresh regs before storing the OP_GETIDX0 Hash result https://github.com/mruby/mruby/pull/7023
## The bug

`vm_op_getidx0()` stores the Hash result through the registers it came in with:

```c
  else if (tt == MRB_TT_HASH) {
    if (mrb_obj_ptr(recv)->c != mrb->hash_class) goto getidx0_fallback;
    regs[a] = mrb_hash_get(mrb, recv, mrb_fixnum_value(0));
    return VM_NEXT;
  }
```

`regs` is `#define regs (ci->stack)`. `mrb_hash_get()` runs the default proc when the key is missing. For a plain `Hash.new { ... }` the `default` method is still the builtin, so `mrb_func_basic_p()` succeeds and the work goes to `hash_default()`, which calls the proc through `mrb_funcall_argv2()`; the `mrb_funcall_argv()` at the end of `mrb_hash_get()` is the other route into the same place, taken when `default` has been overridden. Either way the VM is re-entered, and a proc that pushes enough frames reaches `stack_extend()`, which reallocates `c->stbase` and frees the old buffer.

The destination of the store is `ci->stack + a`, and the C evaluation order for an assignment is unspecified, so the a

Executing the following ruby script causes a heap-use-after-free error. This issue arises from recursive calls to group_by, compounded by the print instruction, which triggers unsafe memory access during object inspection.

When built with `conf.enable_debug` and `conf.defines << %w(MRB_GC_STRESS MRB_HEAP_PAGE_SIZE=169)`, the test in `mruby-enumerator` reports “Use-after-free”.
I went back through the commit log and found that the problem started with commit 5bd63d623. However, I didn't see any problem with the code written.

I don't know where the tail of the cause is, but I will try to find out more.

  enable_test

  defines << %w(MRB_HEAP_PAGE_SIZE=169)

The following was reported by https://hackerone.com/pnoltof:

-----

Root Cause:
==========

calling `File#initilialize_copy` with an invalid argument, causes the function to terminate early, leaving a dangling pointer in the recievers `DATA_PTR`.

```
mrb_io_initialize_copy(mrb_state *mrb, mrb_value copy)
{
  mrb_value orig;
  mrb_value buf;
  struct mrb_io *fptr_copy;
  struct mrb_io *fptr_orig;
  mrb_bool failed = TRUE;

  mrb_get_args(mrb, "o", &orig);
  fptr_copy = (struct mrb_io *)DATA_PTR(copy);
  if (fptr_copy != NULL) {
    fptr_finalize(mrb, fptr_copy, FALSE);
    mrb_free(mrb, fptr_copy);
  }
  fptr_copy = (struct mrb_io *)mrb_io_alloc(mrb);
  fptr_orig = io_get_open_fptr(mrb, orig); #can raise exception

  DATA_TYPE(copy) = &mrb_io_type;
  DATA_PTR(copy) = fptr_copy;
        [....]
}
```
